description:
Israel is marking three years since the 7 October attacks, in which around 1,200 people were killed by Hamas-led attackers and a further 251 hostages were taken back to Gaza. 
 
The commemorations come in the final weeks of a pivotal election campaign. Benjamin Netanyahu’s record on national security is coming under immense scrutiny, amid reports that the government failed to act on warnings in the months leading up to the 2023 attacks – allegations that the prime minister has strongly denied.
 
Tristan Redman speaks to BBC correspondent Jon Donnison, who is in East Jerusalem.

Convicted murderer Christa Pike has woken up and begun speaking from her hospital bed almost a week after authorities in the US state of Tennessee botched her execution, her lawyers said.

She was sent to hospital after surviving two attempts to execute her via lethal injection for the 1995 murder of a 19-year-old she met at a summer camp for troubled teens.

Now her lawyers are asking for answers and for evidence to be preserved. So what happens now?

description:
The onset of sudden, intrusive thoughts led a young woman to falsely fear she was a paedophile. 
 
For years, Molly stayed silent until a social media video suggested it could be a lesser-known symptom of Obsessive Compulsive Disorder. 

Molly has gone from silence to sharing her OCD story online in the hope that others experiencing the same thoughts don't feel alone. 

If you are suffering distress or despair, details of help and support are available at bbc.co.uk/actionline.
title: When your own mind turns against you: Living with intrusive OCD

author: BBC News
description:
Lawyers for US death row inmate Christa Pike are in court today asking a judge to order Tennessee to preserve all evidence from her botched execution last week. 

The emergency motion filed by her legal team could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state over how the failed execution was carried out. 

Pike's lawyers say she is now "conscious and speaking" after surviving two lethal doses of the drug pentobarbital - her lawyer says she continues to receive care while handcuffed in hospital. 

Pike was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

description:
Adaptations, remakes and reboots are all the rage right now, and there’s often one question that crops up - why?
 
Carrie, Prime Video's new TV series based on Stephen King's debut novel, has been no exception.
 
It's not the first time the tale of high school bullies and supernatural powers has been adapted for the screen.
 
Director Brian de Palma's 1976 movie version is a horror classic, with some of its most famous scenes and imagery widely considered iconic within the genre.
 
But the cast and creator of the latest version, which drags Carrie's story forward 50 years into a world of social media, have been telling BBC Newsbeat's Eleanor Doyle why they believe it's still relevant in 2026.

author: BBC News
description:
The French government has suspended the use of stun grenades by police in school protests, as it appeals to students to go back to the classroom.
 
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez has temporarily halted the use of the grenades after a 15-year-old's hand was blown off by a grenade fired by riot police near a school in Northern France. An investigation into the event has been launched.
 
Wider allegations have been made of excessive use of force by police in dealing with the protests which began at the start of October.
 
More schools reopened on Wednesday, although some remained blockaded, after an estimated 250,000 people took to the streets demonstrating over school conditions on Tuesday.

author: BBC News
description:
As Israel marks the third anniversary of the 7 October Hamas attacks, the BBC has visited residents of kibbutz Nir Oz - one of the worst hit places.

Sitting just a mile (1.6km) from the Gaza border, 41 Nir Oz residents and foreign workers were killed along with six people who had fled to the kibbutz from a party nearby. Seventy-six people from the kibbutz were kidnapped to Gaza, including nine bodies. Fourteen of those hostages were taken alive and killed in captivity.

During the October 7 attack, about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage. The ensuing war between Israel and Hamas has killed more than 74,200 people in Gaza according to the Hamas-run health ministry – whose overall figures are seen as accurate by the UN.

author: BBC News
description:
US death row inmate Christa Pike is "conscious and speaking" after surviving a failed execution attempt in the state of Tennessee last week, her lawyers say.
 
Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, according to a statement from her attorneys on Tuesday.
 
She was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995. But Pike survived two lethal injections last Wednesday and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville for treatment, where she remained unconscious while medical staff cleared her body of the injected pentobarbital.
 
An anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team said her survival is highly unusual.
